# Codebase consistency — implementation plan

**Created:** 2026-09-10 (retained original metadata)
**Generated by:** `/prompts/codebase-consistency-audit/orchestrator.md` (original provenance)
**Audit reports:** `/reports/codebase-consistency-audit/`
**Task tracking:** `/tasks/codebase-consistency-audit-tasks.md`
**Documentation review:** 2026-10-24
**Verified revision:** `3f583002482d80ffd1910676bcf7c63e13989b20` on `develop`
**Status:** Historical implementation record and verification plan; not a current all-complete declaration

## Purpose and boundaries

This plan concerns the ThisOneTimeOnAcidCom repository and the memoir website
at `thisonetimeonacid.com`. The previous reference to “Nova News” was incorrect
project attribution. Ash Shaw remains the author of the memoir; legitimate
author references are not project-name mistakes.

This document preserves the technical history of the consistency audits while
separating historical reports, current source observations and proposed work.
It does not authorise runtime changes, dependency changes, manuscript edits,
asset replacement, deployment changes or broader governance cleanup.

The documentation rewrite is tracked in
[TOA-369](https://linear.app/lightspeedwp/issue/TOA-369/docs-plan-remove-obsolete-assumptions-and-refresh-retained-guidance).
Keep this file at its existing location until the location decision in
[TOA-255](https://linear.app/lightspeedwp/issue/TOA-255/refactor-repo-governance-organise-planning-documents)
is approved. Rewriting this file is not approval to move or delete it.

## Evidence and status vocabulary

- **Historical report:** a statement preserved from an earlier audit or plan,
  not independently verified implementation or a current defect.
- **Source observation:** something inspected in the pinned revision; not proof
  of rendered behaviour, passing tests or production deployment.
- **Proposed verification:** work still requiring an appropriate approved scope.
- **Policy conflict:** contradictory instructions that this plan does not settle.

Read [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) and the
reading order in [guidelines/README.md](../guidelines/README.md) before later
implementation. Where prose and implementation disagree, record the difference
rather than silently treating either as proof of completion.

## Current source observations

At the verified revision:

- `src/styles/globals.css` imports all five `tokens/content-*.css` files.
  September's missing-import finding must not be repeated as an unchanged
  current fact.
- The same file defines semantic colour aliases, brand font aliases, shadow,
  border-radius, z-index and fluid-spacing tokens, including extended variants.
  Presence of these definitions does not prove every reference resolves through
  the active stylesheet chain.
- Legacy `--color-*` aliases and the `.button` block remain. The block includes
  fluid padding and a comment preferring `.btn` for new usage.
- `read-more-btn.css` contains fluid default and compact padding, but also a
  literal hover colour. A claim that all component hex values have disappeared
  is therefore not supported.
- `ThemeToggleES5.tsx` contains an `import.meta.env.DEV` console guard. This
  matches an earlier reported change but conflicts with the bundler prohibition.
- `timeline-page.css` consumes `--timeline-accent` and `--cat-neon`;
  `history-page.css` consumes `--cat-hex`. These observations do not establish
  that every former component still supplies the expected values.
- `src/styles/blocks/button-variations.css`, named by the historical plan, is
  absent at this revision. Its old instructions are not a direction to recreate
  the file.
- `package.json` defines build and test commands and declares npm-compatible
  dependencies. Historical package versions and pnpm recommendations are not a
  current maintenance baseline.

These are targeted source checks, not a rerun of all sub-audits. No build,
browser, accessibility, package-health or production checks were performed for
this documentation review.

## Retained June implementation history

The following identifiers retain the original plan's grouping. “Reported”
means the earlier plan described the change as implemented on 2026-06-19;
it does not establish the implementing commit or successful validation.

### CRIT-01 — Shadow, border-radius and z-index tokens

**June references:** E-01, E-02, E-07.

The audit reported unresolved token references in button and interactive CSS.
The plan described adding definitions to `src/styles/globals.css`, including:

- Shadows: `focus-ring`, `neon-sm`, `card-hover`, `neon-pink`, `neon-blue`
  and `neon-purple`.
- Radii: `full`, `circle`, `lg`, `md` and `sm`.
- Layering: `n1`, `0`, `1`, `10`, `100`, `overlay`, `modal` and `toast`.

Those token families are present in the inspected source. For example,
`--wp--preset--border-radius--full` is `9999px`,
`--wp--preset--z-index--overlay` is `1000`, and
`--wp--preset--z-index--modal` is `9000`.

**Verification still needed for a fresh audit:** inspect the actual load chain,
overrides and computed focus, hover and layering behaviour.

### CRIT-02 — Semantic colour aliases

**June references:** E-03, E-04.

The reported change introduced `primary`, `base` and `contrast` aliases, plus
neon-purple and accessible text variants. Current `globals.css` includes:

- `primary` → `neon-pink`.
- `base` → `atomic-black`.
- `contrast` → `text-light`.
- `neon-purple` → `uv-violet`.

Retain the distinction between bright decorative colours and text colours.
Token existence alone does not establish sufficient contrast in either theme.

### CRIT-03 — Brand font and spacing aliases

**June references:** E-05, E-06.

The plan reported adding `brand-heading`, `brand-body`, `brand-title`, numbered
spacing, `fluid-*` spacing and section-padding aliases. These families remain
in `globals.css`.

Representative fluid values include `fluid-md: clamp(1rem, 3vw, 2rem)` and
`section-horizontal: clamp(1.5rem, 6vw, 4rem)`.

A later audit should check consumers and overrides rather than add duplicate
definitions or assume historical font-loading claims remain valid.

### CRIT-04 — Fluid button padding

**June references:** A-01, A-02, A-03.

The historical plan distinguished `.btn`, legacy `.button`,
`.wp-block-button__link` and the standalone read-more button. It proposed
modernising existing consumers without deleting a still-used legacy system.

Current observations preserve two useful examples:

- Legacy `.button`:
  `clamp(0.75rem, 1.5vw, 1rem) clamp(1.5rem, 4vw, 2.5rem)`.
- `.read-more-btn`:
  `clamp(0.5rem, 1.25vw, 0.75rem) clamp(0.875rem, 2.5vw, 1.25rem)`.

The old WordPress-style stylesheet is absent. Resolve current consumers before
any future consolidation; do not restore historical files merely to satisfy
this plan.

### HIGH-01 — Selector colours use tokens

**June reference:** B-01.

Reported replacements covered header navigation, active/hover states, form
errors and primary-button text/hover colours in `globals.css`. Several named
selectors now use token references.

Do not retain the broader implication that every literal colour has been
eliminated: current source still contains literals, including decorative
gradients and a mobile-menu border. Their classification requires contextual
review, not an automatic replacement sweep.

### HIGH-02 — Fluid typography

**June reference:** B-03.

Reported conversions covered `.eyebrow`, `.heading-card`, `.text-body`,
`.text-fine` and `.form__label`. The inspected source contains `clamp()` values
for these selectors.

Retain the intent: responsive typography with usable zoom behaviour. Do not
treat a `clamp()` declaration as proof of accessibility or visual correctness.

### HIGH-03 — Console logging and bundler compatibility

**June reference:** D-01.

The historical change wrapped a theme-toggle log in `import.meta.env.DEV`.
That guard remains in `ThemeToggleES5.tsx`.

The old plan's assertion that React components are exempt from the prohibition
is not supported by the current bundler table. `AGENTS.md` explicitly records
the contradiction and directs contributors not to introduce `import.meta.env`.

**Unresolved:** agree a logging approach compatible with the supported
environments before implementing a replacement. This document does not choose
one or alter the component.

### HIGH-04 — Palette demo structure

**June reference:** C-01.

The plan reported moving static layout, spacing and typography from
`PaletteDemoModal.tsx` into `palette-demo-modal.css`, using `.demo-section`
and `.demo-card` BEM families.

It separately classified live swatch colours, generated gradients and generated
shadows as data-driven exceptions. Preserve that distinction as audit history,
not blanket permission for new inline styles. The complete refactor and its
current consumers were not revalidated during this review.

### HIGH-05 — Theme colour sweep

**June references:** B-02, E-09.

The reported sweep covered `dark.css` and `dark-extended.css`, including body,
header, footer, sidebar, navigation, figure and caption selectors.

Historical examples mapped atomic black, light text, neon pink, muted text and
elevated surfaces to tokens. September reported further theme findings.
Neither report establishes a current zero-literal baseline.

### MED-01 — Timeline dynamic colours

**June reference:** C-02.

The reported approach supplied `--timeline-accent` and `--cat-neon` dynamically,
then consumed them in stylesheet rules for cards, icons, categories and legends.

Those consumers remain in `timeline-page.css`. Confirm the current component
and data path before changing the pattern; do not infer a complete current
integration from CSS alone.

### MED-02 — History legend colours

**June reference:** C-03.

The reported approach supplied `--cat-hex` for legend dots.
`history-page.css` still consumes it with a neon-pink fallback.

Future verification should inspect the supplying component, category mapping and
theme contrast rather than mechanically remove the custom-property boundary.

### MED-03 — Contextual inline-style classifications

**June references:** C-04, C-05.

The historical review classified a data-driven press-kit background image and
slider custom properties in `WhySection.tsx` as exceptions.

Old line numbers are historical locators, not current guarantees. Recheck the
specific expression and applicable policy before relying on an exception.

### MED-04 — Legacy `.button` compatibility

**June reference:** B-05.

The plan reported modernising rather than deleting `.button`, because ebook
components depended on it. The current block has fluid padding, brand font and
radius tokens, and a deprecation comment.

Do not remove it based solely on this history. A future migration needs a
current consumer inventory and regression evidence.

### MED-05 — Dual token aliases

**June references:** B-04, E-08.

The earlier plan retained `--color-*` aliases for compatibility while preferring
`--wp--preset--*` for new token references. Current `globals.css` still contains
that alias layer.

This is not approval for a bulk rename. Check current design-token guidance and
actual consumers before changing either convention.

## Historical exception register

| Pattern or location | Earlier rationale | Present treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Mega-menu/dropdown stagger custom properties | Data-driven animation indices | Retain as historical classification; verify current usage |
| Blog/podcast progress width | Runtime progress value | Distinguish dynamic values from static layout |
| Portfolio/press-kit background image | Data-driven asset URL | Preserve protected images; verify expression and policy |
| Responsive slider flex basis | Computed layout | Review case by case |
| Palette demo colour, gradient and shadow | Live demonstration data | Not a general styling exemption |
| `WhySection` slider properties | Custom-property boundary | Verify supplying values and CSS consumers |
| `ErrorBoundary` logging | Crash reporting | Requires explicit treatment in the logging policy |
| Style-guide example text | Console call shown as a string, not executed | Distinguish examples from executable calls |
| `extensionErrorSuppressor` | Suppression utility | Review purpose before flagging or removing |

The strict no-inline-style wording in `Guidelines.md` differs from the
data-driven exception in `css-architecture.md`. The historical exception list
does not resolve that policy conflict.

## September scope retained for later verification

Do not lose the expanded audit coverage merely because this plan originated
with five domains:

- **H — Backlog:** reconcile existing work before proposing duplicate tasks.
- **F — Packages:** verify current versions, imports and dependency placement.
  The old instruction to switch Netlify to pnpm is superseded by npm-only
  repository guidance.
- **E — Tokens:** verify imports, definitions, aliases, fallbacks and active
  theme overrides; include gradients and aspect ratios where consumed.
- **B/A — Styling and buttons:** inspect colours, typography, padding and
  compatibility across current consumers.
- **C/D — Inline values and logging:** classify runtime values and resolve
  policy conflicts before prescribing changes.
- **G — Web standards:** verify current schema, social assets, crawler files,
  sitemap, font loading, route splitting, image priority, keyboard access and
  deployment headers.

These are retained audit domains, not newly approved implementation tasks.
Historical production-breakage claims require new evidence before being
presented as current findings.

## Unresolved policy and workflow decisions

1. **Planning location:** this file remains under `plan/`. TOA-255 owns any
   approved relocation and reference migration.
2. **Audit output locations:** at the pinned revision, the orchestrator named `src/app/prompts`, `src/app/reports` and `src/app/tasks`. Current `develop` uses root-level `prompts/`, `reports/` and `tasks/` in the orchestrator. Preserve the former paths as historical context; do not create duplicate trees.
3. **Report retention:** guidance contains conflicting immediate and delayed
   archiving/deletion instructions. No report is moved or deleted by this plan.
4. **CSS imports:** the bundler table discourages CSS imports while current
   stylesheets use them. Verify supported-environment behaviour before
   prescribing an import rewrite.
5. **Inline values and logging:** resolve the contradictions described above;
   do not establish new exemptions here.
6. **Tooling claims:** current `package.json` defines tests but no `lint`,
   `type-check`, `typecheck` or `verify` script. Older “no tests” statements and
   historical dependency-removal claims are not a current baseline.
7. **Changelog:** documentation-only applicability remains unresolved in
   TOA-369. `CHANGELOG.md` is protected; no exemption, entry or version bump is
   authorised by this plan.
8. **PR template:** local routing and shared template conventions need
   reconciliation before a PR. Do not claim automatic template insertion or
   alter protected routing/templates as part of these two rewrites.

## Proposed verification and acceptance

After approval to apply the documentation changes:

- Confirm the current `develop` revision and reread any changed instructions.
- Keep the diff limited to the two existing plan files unless separately
  approved.
- Check relative links from their actual `plan/` location; distinguish existing
  references from deliberately historical or absent paths.
- Review the historical identifier/count reconciliation and ensure no inherited
  completion claim is presented as fresh evidence.
- Use the repository's available npm commands for any agreed validation, and
  record exactly what ran, its revision and its result.
- Resolve changelog and PR-template treatment before preparing a PR.
- Do not close implementation issues, alter task checkboxes or claim runtime
  fixes on the strength of a documentation rewrite.

For a separately approved future audit, retain dated reports and use the
eight-domain order above after resolving stale output paths. Record findings
with file/function evidence, distinguish source checks from browser results,
and compare them with existing work before proposing changes.
